newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW plans in-house agency for temp workers - report.
newsitem.headline: VW plans in-house agency for temp workers - report.

text.p: German carmaker Volkswagen AG may set up an in-house employment agency for temporary workers, with the aim of lowering wage costs, a company spokesman said on Wednesday.

VW spokesman Hans-Peter Blechinger told Reuters Europe's largest carmaker could create a services subsidiary that would employ staff at lower wages, to reinforce divisions that faced difficult business conditions.
Volkswagen's works council said the carmaker and labour were already in talks about the possible subsidiary, but that workers were opposed to the plan as it stands so far.

According to the plan, staff managed by the internal agency would be paid according to the industry-wide wage agreement, rather than the more expensive VW wage package where wages are around five marks an hour more than the industry as a whole.
Volkswagen declined to offer details about the plan until the next round of wage talks scheduled to start April 17.
Sources at union IG Metall said the scheme would create a total of 800 to 1,000 new jobs at plants in Hannover, Emden and Kassel.
But works council chief Bernd Sudholt said he opposed the scheme because it would lead to a situation where workers received different pay for performing the same tasks.
IG Metall also opposed the plan. "So long as VW thinks about different pay for the same work, there is nothing to discuss," union spokesman Georgios Arwanitidis said.
The scheme is the latest attempt by Volkswagen to reduce its wage costs.
Volkswagen, Europe's largest carmaker, has in the past tried many ways to make its workforce more flexible so that production could be increased during periods of heavy demand.

The carmaker faces a difficult task in keeping labour costs down because the state government, which owns a 20 percent share in VW, has opposed some attempts by VW to reduce its workforce as other German carmakers have.
The carmaker and unions have met twice to agree a new wage contract, agreeing on March 26 to hold a third round of talks on April 17.
